newsitem.title: USA: Blue chips end firmer, flirt with record highs.
newsitem.headline: Blue chips end firmer, flirt with record highs.

text.p: Wall Street's "Santa Claus" rally spilled over to the day after Christmas Thursday as the Dow Jones industrial average flirted with a record high on the slowest trading day so far this year.

"Maybe it's the Christmas spirit carrying over," said Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer and Co. "It's the usual amount of random noise in the last few sessions of the year. The biggest investors are already done" for 1996, he said.

The Dow industrials rose 23.83 points to 6,546.68, leaving the index of 30 blue-chip stocks just shy of its record of 6,547.79 set on Nov. 25. It was the seventh straight rise for the world's most widely watched stock index.

The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks rose 4.79 points to 755.82, within two points of the record of 757.03, also set on Nov. 25. The Nasdaq Composite index gained 6.94 to 1,294.57, well short of its Dec. 9 record of 1,316.27.
The rally came after the Dow gained nearly 34 points on Tuesday as investors scooped up big-name stocks in what analysts called a traditional Christmas rally.
At the New York Stock Exchange Thursday, winners beat losers, 1,576 to 831, on volume of 253.4 million shares, the lightest full session this year.
The previous slowest full session was 258 million shares on Aug. 30. Volume was 167.2 million in an abbreviated Christmas Eve session on Tuesday. The market was closed on Wednesday for Christmas.
Analysts said blue chips gained as money managers sought to spruce up their portfolios before year-end. They predicted similarly light trading until after the New Year.

"I don't think we'll get much action for the rest of the year with the holidays this week and next week. Brokerages and investment houses are minimally staffed," said Ed Nicoski, a Piper Jaffray technical analyst.

Technology stocks again took the limelight, with Motorola rising 2-3/4 to 63-1/4, Micron adding 1-1/4 to 31-1/4, Compaq Computer up 1-1/8 to 75-3/4, Intel rising 1-1/8 to 136-5/8 and Microsoft up 5/8 to 85-1/2.

Among individual issues, AT&T rose 1-1/2 to 43, boosted by the Federal Communications Commission's proposal for long-distance access charge reform. The proposal to trim the $23 billion long-distance companies pay to local service providers in access fees would benefit AT&T and other long-distance carriers, industry analysts said.
Culbro surged 4-1/4 to 61-7/8. The company plans to sell shares in its General Cigar Holdings unit to the public.
American Express lost 2-1/4 to 56-7/8 and General Electric added 1-1/4 to 103-1/4 after GE reiterated that it was not interested in buying American Express, which declined to comment.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 2.07 points to 397.07. The average share added 22 cents.
The American Stock Exchange index edged up 1.48 to 582.83.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,270.917, up 38.924 points, or 0.54 percent.
